title: BBQ Sausages with Chicken and Pork Kebabs
summary: A full BBQ run on a three-zone grill: fresh beef and pork sausages first, then chicken and pork kebabs, each to a safe temperature.
equipment: BBQ with a lid and a hot, a medium and a cool zone

steps.heading: Set up the BBQ
steps.text: Preheat the BBQ and set up three zones, measured at the grate: hot at {temp:230-260} for browning, medium at {temp:180-210} for the main cooking, and cool at {temp:120-150} for holding food and stopping it burning. Keep the hot zone going throughout.

Plan by space, not by quantity. Each zone takes only one layer with a finger's gap between pieces: crowded food steams instead of browning, and you lose the room to move anything that flares up. Always keep a strip of the cool zone free for that.

steps.heading: Sausages
steps.text: Lay as many sausages on the medium zone as fit in one layer with a gap between each. If they do not all fit, cook them in batches and keep the finished ones on the cool zone. Never start fresh sausages on the hot zone.

Close the lid and cook for {timer:3-4|sausages}. Open it, turn the sausages and close it again. Repeat every 3-4 minutes, for {timer:15-20|sausages total} in all. If they brown too fast, move them to the cool zone.
Once they are almost cooked, move a few at a time to the hot zone with the lid open, turning often, {timer:30-60s} per side, until well browned. Never leave them there unattended: the fat flares up.
They are done at {temp:71!} in the centre of the thickest one. Rest them for {timer:5}. Do not prick them: they lose their juices.

steps.heading: Chicken kebabs
steps.text: Bring the hot zone up to {temp:230-250}. Oil the kebabs lightly, rather than the grill.

Put only as many kebabs on the hot zone as fit with a finger's gap between them, and leave the medium zone clear for them to move onto. With the lid open, turn them every 1-2 minutes for {timer:4-6|chicken sear}, until well browned without burning.
Move them to the medium zone, at {temp:180-200}, close the lid and cook for {timer:3-6|chicken}, turning once or twice. Then sear the next batch on the hot zone.
Take each one off as soon as the middle of the largest piece reaches {temp:74!}, so it does not dry out.

steps.heading: Pork kebabs
steps.text: Bring the hot zone back up to {temp:230-250}. Sear the pork kebabs on it, as many as fit with gaps, lid open, turning every 1-2 minutes for {timer:4-6|pork sear}.

Move them to the medium zone, close the lid and cook until the centre reaches at least {temp:63!}, or {temp:68-70!} if you like it more done. Small pieces take 8-12 minutes in all. Rest them for at least {timer:3}.

tips: In short: sausages on medium with the lid closed; kebabs seared on hot with the lid open, then finished on medium with the lid closed.
Keep raw chicken, raw pork and the raw sausages away from cooked food, with their own plates and tongs. Never put cooked meat back on a plate that held raw meat.
Soak wooden skewers in water for at least 30 minutes before threading them.
A thermometer in the lid reads differently from the heat at the grate where the food is, so treat it only as a guide.
Kebabs with vegetables need turning more often, so the vegetables do not burn before the meat is cooked.
